description:
Render a document, or the model it evaluates to. The same request can be
executed locally or sent to a remote `cadpole serve` for offloading.

analysis.description:
Colour-map a measured field over the surface instead of the bodies'
materials, with a legend drawn into the image (docs/views.md, "Analysis
views"). "thickness" is wall thickness against the minimum below;
"overhang" is the angle from vertical against the support threshold.
Empty renders materials normally.

backdrop.description:
The surround: "studio" (a grey cyclorama with a soft top light),
"white", "black" or "#rrggbb". Sets the environment the path tracer
shows and reflects, the colour of its floor, and — unless `background`
is given — the rasterizer's background to the same tone, so the two
backends agree. Empty keeps the rig's own gradient, the dark floor and
the default background.

background.description:
Colour of the pixels the model does not cover, linear RGB in 0..1
(unset = the default dark grey). Written bit-exactly, so a contact sheet
or a page background matches.

bloom.description:
Bloom: highlights over display white spill a little into their
neighbours, so an LED reads as a light and a specular ping bleeds a
pixel or two. Off by default because the halo crosses the silhouette
and the backdrop next to it stops being bit-exactly `background`.

body_ids.description: Body ids to render; empty for all visible bodies.

boolean_tolerance.description:
Boolean (kernel) tolerance in mm (0 = engine default). Separate from
`tolerance` because kernel cost grows sharply as it shrinks.

camera.description:
Camera for rendering. Either a named preset or explicit eye/target: with
`preset` empty and `eye` set the camera stands exactly there and looks at
`target` (`cadpole render --eye x,y,z --target x,y,z`) -- a neighbour's
window, a point on the sidewalk -- and nothing is fitted to the model.
Both empty takes the document's `render_defaults(camera=)`, else `iso`.

fit_margin.description: Extra padding around the fitted model, as a fraction of its size.

preset.description:
A named direction, an angle pair, or "" when eye/target are given instead.

Names: "iso", "front", "back", "top", "bottom", "left", "right",
"iso-bottom" (looking up at the underside from a corner, which is how you
inspect a printed base) and "iso-back".

Angles: "az=<degrees>,el=<degrees>". Azimuth turns from the front view
toward the right; elevation is above the horizon, so negative looks up
from below. Either may be left out. "iso" is "az=45,el=29.5".

debug.description:
Draw a debug view of the mesh instead of the part (docs/views.md, "Debug
views"): "faces" colours every topology face group, so a boolean that
shattered its faces shows as noise; "normals" paints the shading normal
as RGB, so a surface that should read smooth shows its facets; "defects"
paints the triangles the solid validator flags (crossings red, slivers
orange, folds magenta) over a grey body and reports the counts as an
info diagnostic; "seams" draws feature edges classified by the crease
rule (creases black, smoothed seams blue); "wire" draws every triangle
edge over a faint body. Debug views are flat-lit, opaque and rasterized
at one sample whatever `backend`, `samples` or `xray` say, so nothing
gets between the reading and the eye. Empty renders the part normally;
cannot be combined with `analysis`.

denoise.description:
Path tracing: an edge-aware à-trous denoise of the finished image,
guided by the first hit's normal, albedo and depth. Removes the grain
that remains on glossy metals at a few hundred samples; also softens
fine texture below the noise level, so use it for a still, not for
judging a surface finish. Off by default.

dof_f_number.description:
Path tracing: thin-lens depth of field at this f-number, focused on the
model (a real lens for the field of view: f/8 on a 60 mm part is a
gentle fall-off at the far edge of the floor, f/4 a hero shot). 0 is a
pinhole, the default.

draft.description:
Fast preview: samples = 1 (unless `samples` is set), no ambient
occlusion, no contact shadow.

edge_break_mm.description:
Path tracing: shade every crease edge as if it carried an edge break of
this radius in mm (0 = none, the default; 0.25 is a typical machined
deburr), so edges catch the light as the narrow bright lines a real
part shows instead of reading razor-sharp. No geometry is changed: the
shading normal near a crease is blended toward the neighbouring face.
A material's own `edge_break` overrides it for that body.

edge_crease_degrees.description:
Minimum angle between the surfaces meeting at an edge, in degrees, for
the raster overlay to draw that edge (0 = the default 30). Tangent seams
between the patches of one smooth surface measure ~0 degrees and are
never drawn.

edge_mode.description: Which static edges to draw (unset = EDGE_MODE_CREASES).

edge_width_px.description:
Feature-edge width in pixels (0 = the default 1.15), independent of
resolution and of the sample count.

exposure.description: Exposure multiplier applied before the tonemap (0 = default 1.0).

floor.description:
Path tracing: the floor's finish. "matte" (the default) is the matte
sweep; "gloss" reflects the part faintly, as a slightly glossy table
does in a product photograph; "none" removes the floor.

grid_mode.description:
Ground grid style (unset = GRID_MODE_INFINITE). `draw_grid = false`
still turns the grid off.

highlight_selection.description:
Draw the document's selection in the highlight colour (annotated
screenshot for an assistant).

layers.description:
Display layers for this image: `envelope=off` hides a layer,
`terrain=0.4` ghosts one at 40 % opacity, `envelope=on` shows a layer
the script declared hidden; one entry per `--layer`. A layer not named
here keeps its own `layer(visible=, opacity=)` defaults.

items.description:
A display-layer override for one render: the layer by name and
what to change about it. A field left unset keeps the layer's own default
from `layer(...)`. The empty name is the implicit layer of untagged bodies
(`cadpole render --layer other=off`, unless the script declares a layer
called `other`).

opacity.description:
Draw them at this opacity, 0..1: below 1 they are ghosted, translucent
the way `material(opacity=)` is, on every backend.

visible.description: Draw the layer's bodies at all.

lighting.description:
The light rig (docs/views.md, "The product shot"). "studio" (the
default, and the look of every image before it): a warm key from the
front-left in world space, a cool fill, a rim from behind — the
engineering look, which reads form well but lights a `back` view from
behind. "product": a neutral catalogue rig that turns with the camera —
key 40° to camera-left and 40° up, a large soft fill 55° to the right,
a narrow rim behind — over a brighter grey surround, so a white part
renders white and a glossy face has something to reflect. Both
backends honour it.

max_bounces.description:
Path tracing: maximum surface scattering events per path (0 = the
default 8). Russian roulette usually ends a path well before this.
Ignored by the rasterizer.

max_overhang_degrees.description:
Overhang angle from vertical, in degrees, past which a surface needs
support, for `analysis = "overhang"` (0 = 45).

min_wall.description:
Minimum wall thickness in mm for `analysis = "thickness"` (0 = two
perimeters of a 0.4 mm nozzle, i.e. 0.8). The ramp is anchored on it:
red below, amber at it, blue well above.

no_edges.description:
Turn feature edges off. proto3 cannot tell "false" from "unset", and
`draw_edges`/`draw_grid` both false means "defaults" (both on), so
switching one off explicitly needs its own flag.

no_grid.description: Turn the ground grid off. See `no_edges`.

north_degrees.description:
Where north is in model space, in degrees clockwise from +y seen from
above: 0 means +y is north (the default), 90 means +x is north. 0
defers to the document's `render_defaults(north=)`, if any.

param_overrides.description: Param overrides applied on top of the document's, for sweeps.

samples.description:
Raster: anti-aliasing samples per pixel (0 = default 4; 1, 4 or 8).
Path tracing: samples per pixel.

section.description:
Cut every body by a plane for this image only, with the cut capped:
`x=22` removes everything on the +x side of x = 22 (`y=`, `z=`
likewise), and `-x=22` removes the -x side instead. A body the mesh
kernel cannot cut (not watertight) is drawn whole, with a warning.
Empty renders the bodies whole.

shadow_catcher.description:
With `transparent`: keep the shadow the model casts on the ground, as
black at the alpha of the light it blocks, and nothing else of the
ground. Path tracing catches the rig's and the sky's shadow; the
rasterizer its contact shadow.

show_environment.description:
Path tracing: where a camera ray hits nothing, show the studio's
environment gradient (the sky the lights and the reflections come from)
instead of the flat `background` colour. Off by default so a path-traced
image and a rasterized one share a backdrop; on, a metal or a glass has
something visible to reflect. Ignored by the rasterizer.

sun.description:
The sun: a directional light with sharp shadows added to the
rig. `lat,lon,YYYY-MM-DD,HH:MM[,tz]` computes it for a place, a date
and a local clock time (NOAA's algorithm, to half a degree; the zone
defaults to the longitude's standard zone with no daylight saving), or
`az=<deg>,el=<deg>` places it by compass azimuth (0 north, 90 east,
clockwise) and elevation above the horizon. Empty is no sun of the
request's own: the document's `render_defaults(sun=)` if it declares
one, else the rig alone. A sun below the horizon lights nothing.

supersample.description:
Render at this many times the size in each direction and filter down
(1 to 4; 0 = 1). For edges finer than the samples resolve: thin
features, and the rasterizer's fixed 8 positions per pixel. Costs the
square of it in the rasterizer; the path tracer spreads the same
`samples` over the finer grid.

threads.description: Raster worker threads (0 = auto). Never changes the output.

tonemap.description:
The tone curve. "aces" (the default) is the ACES fit every image has
had; "neutral" is Khronos PBR Neutral — hue-preserving and exact for
base colours under unit light, the product-shot choice — and "none" a
plain clamp.

transparent.description:
Leave the backdrop out: pixels the model does not cover are written
with alpha 0, and an edge pixel's alpha is the share of it the model
covers, measured by the same samples as its colour. The PNG is straight
(unpremultiplied) alpha and the colour stored at an edge is the
model's own, so the image composites over any colour without a fringe.
The environment still lights and reflects in the model; `background`,
the floor and (path tracing) `show_environment` are not drawn. Glass
and translucent bodies are partly transparent. The ground grid, when
drawn, is ink at its own alpha.

xray.description: Draw every body translucent so interiors and overlaps are visible.

title: Render one image of a document
